name: Office Application Startup

attack_mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program

evidence.rationale: Application patches can restrict specific Outlook startup and persistence mechanisms, including Outlook Forms, Home Page, and Rules. Other Office startup mechanisms that rely on macros, add-ins, templates, or configuration changes are not necessarily prevented by patching.

This is a partial parent mapping because product remediation can restrict specific Outlook startup and persistence mechanisms, including Outlook Forms, Home Page, and Rules. Other Office startup methods may require configuration and application-control safeguards.

This is a partial mapping because several sub-techniques specifically abuse Outlook features addressed by vendor patches. Other Office startup methods involving templates, test keys, and general add-ins are outside the browser-and-email-client scope.
Restricting email-client add-ins mitigates the add-in portion of this parent technique.

Host-based intrusion prevention capabilities can enforce Attack Surface Reduction rules that prevent Office applications from creating child processes or writing potentially malicious executable content to disk.

limits: A claim shows that a control can mitigate a technique. It does not show that an implementation is effective.
'none' or 'no_row' means the mapping has no mitigating control. It does not mean that no defence exists.
Claims use ATT&CK Enterprise 16.1, the version that the source mapping uses. See later_version for changes in newer versions.
CIS claims (cis_claims and cis/safeguards) use ATT&CK Enterprise 19.1, the version that the CIS mapping uses.

ATLAS data is version 5.6.0, the legacy ATLAS file. It is not the current ATLAS release (v2026.10 on 2026-11-08). An empty mitigation list means that ATLAS 5.6.0 links no mitigation, not that no mitigation exists. agent_related is derived by this project from names.
